note: Dolutegravir, bictegravir and cabotegravir went into patients on cell-culture antiviral potency with a protein-adjusted IC90/IC95 trough target and standard rat/rabbit reproductive toxicology.
label: HIV integrase inhibitors

engagement.note: Dolutegravir blocked HIV replication in cell assays at low-nanomolar potency; this assay was the class's engagement readout.
engagement.short: Low-nM block of HIV in cells
engagement.quote: In a variety of cellular antiviral assays, S/GSK1349572 inhibited HIV replication with low-nanomolar or subnanomolar potency and with a selectivity index of 9,400.
engagement.judgement: Strip opens at the first public cell-culture paper for a member drug (epub Nov 2010); the drug had entered patients in 2008 (NCT00708110), so 2010 is a proxy. Raltegravir/elvitegravir work is not used: not members.

engagement.note: Ten days of dolutegravir monotherapy cut plasma HIV-1 RNA 1.5-2.5 log10 with a clear dose-response, as the cell assay predicted.
engagement.short: Viral load fell up to 2.5 log10
engagement.quote: Significant reductions in plasma HIV-1 RNA from baseline to day 11 were observed for all DTG dose groups compared with placebo (P < 0.001), with a mean decrease of 1.51-2.46 log(10) copies/ml.
engagement.reason: Viral load fell in dosed patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: viral-load decline vs in-vitro replication inhibition
engagement.judgement: Viral load is the target's own product (proximal tier). Paired by me: the monotherapy abstract does not set out the cell data. Bictegravir (Gallant 2017, 10.1097/QAI.0000000000001306, 1.45-2.43 log10) and cabotegravir (Spreen 2013, 10.1310/hct1405-192) monotherapy studies agree and change no status.

dose.model: Protein-adjusted cell-culture potency as plasma trough target
dose.note: Serum-adjusted cell potency (PA-EC50 38 nM; PA-IC90 64 ng/mL) set the plasma trough the human dose had to clear.
dose.quote: The protein-adjusted half-maximal effective concentration (PA-EC(50)) extrapolated to 100% human serum was 38 nM.
dose.judgement: The PA-IC90 of 0.064 ug/mL is taken from the FDA clinical pharmacology review; the paper's abstract gives PA-EC50 only.

dose.model: Protein-adjusted cell-culture potency as plasma trough target
dose.note: FDA: dolutegravir 50 mg troughs sat 19-fold above the cell PA-IC90 and on the Emax plateau; the dose worked in Phase 3.
dose.quote: The 50 mg once daily dose achieved an inhibitory quotient of 19, providing considerable coverage above the target concentration of 0.064 ng/ml (protein-adjusted IC90).
dose.confidence_note: quote verbatim from the review, whose 'ng/ml' is a typo for ug/mL
dose.magnitude_basis: trough / PA-IC90 inhibitory quotient vs virologic response
dose.judgement: 'Reached, drug worked' row. direction_only because the target did not tell doses apart: SPRING-1 found 10, 25 and 50 mg equally effective at week 48, and 50 mg was chosen for interaction and adherence headroom. The 50 mg BID dose for INSTI-resistant virus belongs to a resistant population and is not scored. Bictegravir (paIQ95 ~20 at 75 mg, FDA multidiscipline review 210251) and cabotegravir LA (4x PA-IC90 target, FLAIR/ATLAS) followed the same yardstick with no dose failure in treatment. The cabotegravir 800 mg Q12W PrEP regimen missing 4x PA-IC90 (FDA 215499 review) was in HIV-negative people and was an error of human PK projection, so it is not scored.

efficacy.note: Cell-culture replication assays, with resistance passage, were the efficacy model; no animal infection model was on the treatment path.
efficacy.short: Cell replication assay is the model
efficacy.quote: S/GSK1349572 is a next-generation HIV integrase (IN) inhibitor designed to deliver potent antiviral activity with a low-milligram once-daily dose requiring no pharmacokinetic (PK) booster.
efficacy.judgement: The SHIV-macaque challenge models (Andrews 2014; Markowitz 2015) were relied on for cabotegravir PrEP in HIV-negative people, not for treating patients of this disease, so they are excluded.

efficacy.note: SPRING-1 primary endpoint: 93% on dolutegravir vs 60% on efavirenz below 50 copies/mL at week 16.
efficacy.quote: Week 16 response rates to viral loads of at most 50 copies per mL were 93% (144 of 155 participants) for all doses of dolutegravir (with little difference between dose groups) and 60% (30 of 50) for efavirenz
efficacy.magnitude_basis: virologic suppression vs in-vitro antiviral potency
efficacy.judgement: Earliest member-drug trial with a primary virologic endpoint (Phase 2b, epub Oct 2011). Bictegravir (Trial 1489) and cabotegravir LA (FLAIR) Phase 3 trials agree and are listed as patient_trials. No member failed for efficacy, so neg is not available.

efficacy.note: Site-directed raltegravir-resistant clones (Y143R, Q148K, N155H, G140S/Q148H) stayed within 1.1-2.6-fold of wild-type dolutegravir susceptibility.
efficacy.quote: S/GSK1349572 demonstrated activity against site-directed molecular clones containing the raltegravir-resistant signature mutations Y143R, Q148K, N155H, and G140S/Q148H (FCs, 1.4, 1.1, 1.2, and 2.6, respectively)
efficacy.judgement: A distinct use of the cell-culture platform: the mutant panel predicts which resistance genotypes still respond, so it is a patient-level track apart from the draft's wild-type potency track. The FDA review (MedR 2013) discusses these in-vitro mutant data.
efficacy.model: In-vitro susceptibility of INSTI-resistant HIV-1 (site-directed mutant clones, fold-change)

efficacy.note: VIKING: raltegravir-resistant patients responded to dolutegravir; 96% met the day-11 primary endpoint on 50 mg twice daily, as the mutant panel predicted.
efficacy.quote: More subjects achieved the primary end point in cohort II (23 of 24 [96%]), compared with cohort I (21 of 27 [78%]) at day 11.
efficacy.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; the abstract opens with the in-vitro cross-resistance claim, the per-genotype breakdown is in the full text and the FDA review

patient_trials.quote: Multivariate analyses demonstrated a strong association between baseline DTG susceptibility and response. Response was most reduced in subjects with Q148 + ≥2 resistance-associated mutations.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: in-vitro fold-change in DTG susceptibility vs virologic response by baseline genotype/phenotype
efficacy.judgement: comparison_stated true: the VIKING abstract sets the in-vitro limited cross-resistance beside the clinical response. VIKING-3 (2014) and the FDA medical review (2013: 'As expected, response was influenced by fold change susceptibility to DTG') confirm the per-phenotype gradient (72% <3-fold, 22% >=10-fold), so the status holds. The Q148+>=2 secondary pathway responded poorly; the panel's G140S/Q148H double mutant (2.6-fold) did not show how bad the triple-mutant pathway would be, which I treat as magnitude, not direction.
efficacy.model: In-vitro susceptibility of INSTI-resistant HIV-1 (site-directed mutant clones, fold-change)

safety.model: Rat and rabbit embryo-fetal development studies
safety.note: Dolutegravir caused no developmental toxicity or malformations in rats at ~27x human exposure; the rabbit study reached only 0.4x.
safety.quote: Oral administration of dolutegravir to pregnant rats at doses up to 1,000 mg/kg daily, approximately 27 times the 50-mg twice-daily human clinical exposure based on AUC, from days 6 to 17 of gestation did not elicit maternal toxicity, developmental toxicity, or teratogenicity.
safety.judgement: The FDA pharmacology review (204790Orig1s000PharmR) gives the rat embryo-fetal NOAEL as 1000 mg/kg/day. Bictegravir and cabotegravir reproductive packages were also clean and have no human counter-signal.

safety.model: Rat and rabbit embryo-fetal development studies
safety.note: Tsepamo: neural-tube defects in 0.30% of births with dolutegravir at conception vs 0.10% on other ART, a harm the rat studies did not show.
safety.quote: The prevalence of neural-tube defects was higher in association with dolutegravir treatment at conception than with non-dolutegravir ART at conception (difference, 0.20 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.01 to 0.59)
safety.magnitude_basis: NTD prevalence difference vs no teratogenicity in rats
safety.judgement: Rats can show neural-tube defects, so the silence counts as a miss. The signal was first public in a 2018 NEJM letter (Zash 2018, 10.1056/NEJMc1807653) that I could not quote, so the entry is dated to the 2019 full report.

safety.model: Rat and rabbit embryo-fetal development studies
safety.note: Complete Tsepamo data to 2022: 0.11% NTDs with dolutegravir at conception vs 0.10% on other ART; the early signal fell to background.
safety.quote: No detectable increase in neural tube defects or major external structural abnormalities was noted among more than 11 000 exposures to dolutegravir at conception captured in the Tsepamo Study from 2014 to 2022.
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; PubMed lists a 2027 print date that looks like an indexing error, Crossref gives 2026-11
safety.magnitude_basis: NTD prevalence difference (-0.02%) vs no teratogenicity in rats
safety.judgement: Rule (b) of decision 6: a tier 1 source from the same surveillance shows the early signal attenuated to background. Kourtis 2023 (10.1016/S2352-3018(23)00108-X, US claims) also found no NTD increase earlier, but in another population, so it does not show this signal attenuating. Other class harms (INSTI weight gain, DTG creatinine rise from OCT2 inhibition) were not checked against the tox packages.

safety.note: In vitro, dolutegravir inhibited OCT2, the tubular creatinine secretion transporter, predicting a creatinine rise without loss of filtration.
safety.quote: In vitro, DTG inhibited the renal organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2, IC50=1.9 µM or 0.82 µg/mL).
safety.judgement: First-use year is a proxy: the in-vitro OCT2 data were first public with Koteff 2013 and the 2013 filing.
safety.model: In-vitro renal OCT2 transporter inhibition assay

safety.note: Iohexol and PAH clearance unchanged on dolutegravir; only creatinine clearance fell 10-14%, matching benign OCT2 inhibition predicted in vitro.
safety.short: GFR unchanged; creatinine rise is OCT2
safety.quote: These findings support in vitro data that DTG increases serum creatinine by the benign inhibition of the organic cation transporter 2, which is responsible for tubular secretion of creatinine.
safety.magnitude_basis: measured GFR (iohexol) unchanged vs creatinine clearance -10-14%
safety.judgement: The creatinine rise itself was seen in trials before the OCT2 explanation was proposed (ClinPharmR: 'The applicant hypothesized'), but what the model predicted that was not yet known, no true loss of filtration, was tested prospectively with iohexol, so retrodiction false. Healthy volunteers; the FDA medical review reached the same conclusion for patients in the Phase 3 trials. Bictegravir and cabotegravir carry the same OCT2/MATE1 creatinine labelling, not checked here.
safety.model: In-vitro renal OCT2 transporter inhibition assay

safety.note: Mice dosed with dolutegravir from conception at human-therapeutic and 5x peak levels, built after the Tsepamo neural-tube signal.
safety.quote: Pregnant C57BL/6J mice were randomly allocated to control (water), 1x-DTG (2.5 mg/kg-peak plasma concentration ~3000 ng/ml - therapeutic level), or 5x-DTG (12.5 mg/kg-peak plasma concentration ~12,000 ng/ml - supratherapeutic level)
safety.judgement: Opening entry marking when the model existed. Academic (NIH-funded) model run after the 2018-2019 Tsepamo reports, so every scored comparison on this track is a retrodiction.
safety.model: Pregnant C57BL/6J mice dosed from conception at therapeutic DTG exposure

safety.note: Five NTDs, all at therapeutic DTG, none at 5x; authors match the rate to Tsepamo's 2019 signal.
safety.short: Mice reproduce the Tsepamo NTD signal
safety.quote: Our findings support a causal relationship of DTG at therapeutic doses with increased risk for fetal defects, including NTDs at a rate that is similar that reported in the Tsepamo study for women exposed to DTG-based ART from conception.
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; five NTDs in 1174 fetuses, small numbers
safety.magnitude_basis: NTD rate in 1x-DTG fetuses vs Tsepamo DTG-at-conception prevalence, as the authors state
safety.judgement: Reproduced the human signal known at the time, so retro, not same. GSK's letter (Romach 2021, 10.1016/j.ebiom.2021.103335) disputes the study; not scored.
safety.model: Pregnant C57BL/6J mice dosed from conception at therapeutic DTG exposure

safety.note: With more Tsepamo births the dolutegravir NTD rate fell to 0.10% vs 0.11% on other ART: the harm the mice reproduced is not there.
safety.short: Human NTD signal gone; mouse harm unconfirmed
safety.quote: This difference diminished with subsequent data, with updated estimates of 0.10% for DTG and 0.11% for non-DTG exposures.
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; confirmed by Zash 2026 (10.1016/j.langlo.2026.104076), already in the tile
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse NTD excess at therapeutic DTG vs no NTD excess in final Tsepamo data
safety.judgement: A predicted harm that did not appear in patients is a wrong prediction (contra, opposite). The same group's 2025 mouse comparison (Mohan, 10.1093/infdis/jiaf362) found NTDs with every INSTI including bictegravir and cabotegravir, with no human counter-signal; that does not change the status. Kept retrodiction true because the model was never run ahead of the human data.
safety.model: Pregnant C57BL/6J mice dosed from conception at therapeutic DTG exposure

safety.note: Pregnant CD-1 mice on normal or low folic-acid diets dosed with dolutegravir at human-therapeutic-equivalent and supratherapeutic doses, built after the Tsepamo signal.
safety.quote: They were treated with water, a human therapeutic-equivalent dose, or supratherapeutic dose of DTG from mouse embryonic day E6.5 to E12.5.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. A folate-sensitised mouse (CD-1, low-folate diet) is a different system from the C57BL/6J therapeutic-dose track: NTDs appear only when folate is low. Published ahead of print June 2023 (PMID 37382903, Crossref record 2023-06-29); issue 2024.
safety.model: Folate-deficient pregnant CD-1 mice dosed with DTG (nutrient-sensitised NTD model)

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; NTD counts not in the abstract
safety.note: Exencephaly appeared at therapeutic-equivalent DTG only in low-folate dams; the authors offer it as an explanation of the Botswana NTD signal.
safety.quote: it is possible that DTG exposures in people living with HIV with low folate status during pregnancy may explain, at least in part, the elevated NTD risk signal observed in Botswana.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence of DTG-induced NTDs in low-folate mice vs Tsepamo NTD excess
safety.judgement: Run after the 2018-2019 Tsepamo reports, so retro. Gelineau-van Waes 2023 (10.3389/fcell.2023.1175917) found the same with hypomagnesemic strains (LM/Bc) and low-Mg diets; same sensitised-mouse concept, not scored separately.
safety.model: Folate-deficient pregnant CD-1 mice dosed with DTG (nutrient-sensitised NTD model)

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level reading; Botswana folate status inferred from lack of fortification, not measured in the source
safety.note: With more Tsepamo births the DTG NTD rate fell to 0.10% vs 0.11% on other ART, in an unfortified, low-folate population: the harm the sensitised mice showed did not appear.
safety.quote: This difference diminished with subsequent data, with updated estimates of 0.10% for DTG and 0.11% for non-DTG exposures.
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse NTDs at therapeutic DTG under low folate vs no NTD excess in final Tsepamo data
safety.judgement: First test after the model was built, so retrodiction false; patient_signal_reversed is the turn-back flag for a model that predicted no harm, so false here. Confirmed by Zash 2026 (10.1016/j.langlo.2026.104076).
safety.model: Folate-deficient pregnant CD-1 mice dosed with DTG (nutrient-sensitised NTD model)
